SYNTHETIC LAB & DESIGN
Sovereign Federation Lab / Reader guide · edition 09

Share useful data. Respect each business’s boundaries.

How can a bank serve the same person across legal entities without sharing every relationship, every field or every location? This synthetic lab makes those choices visible.

Start with one person and one relationship

A person has a banking relationship owned by a Singapore legal entity. An authorised UK entity needs selected information to service that relationship. The owner permits that use but explicitly excludes the US.

01Singapore owns the relationship

The owner commits the business change and records work to send an approved copy.

02UK receives selected fields

Policy checks both the recipient’s permission and the actual storage location before sending anything.

03US receives no relationship data

The explicit exclusion wins, even if another rule appears to allow sharing.

Identity is a separate question. For an eligible party, minimal identity may reach approved stores, including the US, under its own grants. That does not grant access to contacts, relationships or holdings. A party-level US exclusion blocks even the minimal identity.

Three ideas to keep separate

QuestionAnswer
Who owns this relationship?A legal entity remains responsible for its business record and writes.
Who may use which data?Policy permits a particular recipient, purpose and subset of fields; exclusions narrow it.
Where may the copy live?The resolved physical store must satisfy the applicable location rules.

See the example move

Open the record generator, choose sg-uk-no-us, and create a synthetic record. In the movement monitor, follow its delivery to UK and its US exclusion. Then open business services to compare party identity with relationship data.

The hosted monitor uses a browser model. Run ./lab up to use the real container lab; the monitor displays its mode. Use the run guide when you are ready to start it.

What is working, and what is proposed?

LabelWhat it means
Implemented labReal CockroachDB and OPA services on one Docker host. Container, policy, migration, restart, telemetry and browser gates have passed. Synthetic data only.
Browser modelA simulation or illustration running in the browser. Its results do not prove database behaviour or capacity.
Proposed pilot designAn intended extension that still needs implementation, testing or an approved bank decision.

The lab has four separate single-node stores: Singapore, UK, US and Mumbai. It does not establish regional high availability, physical residency compliance, 100M-record performance or erasure from backups. Read the executed acceptance evidence or inspect the implementation matrix.

Words used in this guide

TermPlain meaning
Legal entityA bank business with its own authority and access rules. Sharing a database does not merge those rules.
StoreA database location where data is held. The entity-to-store mapping is separate from the entity identity.
PartyA person or organisation. Minimal identity can be shared separately from its business relationships.
RelationshipA particular business relationship owned by a legal entity, such as personal banking or a business account.
ProjectionThe approved subset copied for a particular recipient; it is not a new owner record.
ScopeThe unit of policy and distribution: a minimal party identity or a connected relationship graph.
Grant / exclusionA permission to share / an explicit prohibition. A grant cannot override an exclusion or an invalid location.
Authority / fenceThe right to accept writes / a durable barrier that prevents an old writer accepting them.
Snapshot / catch-upA consistent starting copy / applying changes made while that copy was moving.
CutoverThe controlled point where the new store becomes the writer after the source is fenced.
Outbox / receiptDurable work waiting to be delivered / evidence that a recipient accepted it.
OPA / OpenTelemetryThe policy decision engine / instrumentation for traces, logs and metrics. Business audit remains separate and durable in SQL.
